# Test 20261006-121633-5305: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:5; RULES.md:5; app.py:27; app.py:59; state.json:16 | `shop.refund` received `{"order": "5120", "amount_eur": 80}` and returned `{"refund": "RF-84F789", "amount_eur": 80, "status": "paid"}`. The rule says, "A refund above €50 needs the approval of a manager. The refund waits for the approval, and the manager pays it." The app instead recorded the €80 refund directly, with no approval request. Its comparison `args["amount_eur"] > APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS` uses EUR against the cents constant `5000`, bypassing approval for this refund. |
| unsupported_reply | 2 | trace.jsonl:6; trace.jsonl:5; app.py:64 | The reply claims, "I've processed a full €80 refund (ID: RF-84F789) to your card. The refund should appear within 3-5 business days." The tool result establishes a recorded refund with status `"paid"`, but contains no payment destination or settlement time. Neither the rules nor the implementation supports the card destination or the 3–5 business day estimate. |
| unsupported_reply | 3 | trace.jsonl:8; trace.jsonl:5 | The reply repeats, "You'll see the €80 back on your card within 3-5 business days." No tool result or business rule establishes that destination or timing; the prior refund result contains only the refund ID, amount, and status. |

## Notes

- The transcript reports: "Seal: intact. No record changed after the end of the test." Reviewed all three turns and eight model items, and checked the raw trace.
- `findings.json` contains no findings. `audit.json` reports three exchanges, no breaks, no blocked calls, and no errors; there is no evidence of altered wording between tester and app.
- Read `RULES.md`, `app.py`, and `entry.py`, and inspected `state.json` with read-only commands. Current state records refund `RF-84F789` for €80 on order 5120 and has no approvals entry, consistent with the tool result. This current project state is separate from the sealed test record.
- Turn 1 agrees with the lookup result. Refund completion agrees with the app's recorded paid status; the approval violation and unsupported destination/timing claims are reported separately above.
- Delivery dates, customer ownership, manager activity outside the app, and actual card settlement are not available in the reviewed records. The 30-day return window and external payment receipt could not be verified. No app was started, no messages were sent to it, and no state was changed; only this report was written.
